title: The Tent Rehearsal
clue: A dress rehearsal for a trip that has not happened yet, and your dog reads the reviews.
reveal: A dress rehearsal for a real camping trip, such as the camping adventure in this collection. Test each piece of kit one at a time in a shelter, even the zip. What your dog settles with goes in the trip bag; what worries them stays home.
objective: Test your trip kit one piece at a time in a tent or blanket shelter, pack only what your dog accepted and tag the bag.
instructions: Before you start, write your planned kit (tent, mat, blanket, lantern, bowl) on paper and cut it into slips. Add the question: would you take two beds, or one? Anticipation is part of this.

Set up a tent in a secure yard, or a blanket shelter over two chairs indoors. Keep the door fully open and never zip your dog in, stakes and guy lines marked or out of paths, and give your dog space to walk away.
Add one piece of kit at a time, placed where your dog can reach it, then sit back and wait. For beds, offer two: a mat and a folded blanket.
Let your dog sniff, step in, lie down or avoid it. Do not coax them in. If they back away, take the piece out.
Test the sounds from a distance with your dog free to leave: unzip the door once and crinkle the mat. If ears flatten or your dog leaves, mark that piece Maybe next time.
Sort the slips into three piles: Trip Bag (they settled or sniffed calmly), Stays Home (they avoided it) and Maybe next time (unsure).
If all is calm, sit in the doorway for ten minutes with the lantern dim and the door open, reading while your dog does as they please.
Pack only the Trip Bag pile into a real bag and write a luggage tag listing the dog-approved gear. Take the tent down with your dog free to watch from a blanket, then let them rest.
twist: Your dog gets a veto over every piece of gear, including the zip, and the packing list on the luggage tag is whatever survived.
variations: Indoor or short version: a blanket tent over two chairs in a room, no stakes or yard needed, or test only the mat and the open door in daylight without the lantern.
Seated version: ask a helper to set up the shelter and sit with your dog while they test the kit.

Camp Rules version, at dusk after the test: spend a few minutes watching your dog and note three habits (where they settle, when they wind down, what helps). Write them as three Camp Rules in your dog's voice, read them softly, and make a camp patch from a cardboard circle or fabric scrap to hang on their bed or your leash hook. Sleep in your own beds; battery lights only.

Real campsite upgrade, the camping adventure (optional, about $20 to $300, needs a car): book a dog-welcoming pitch or cabin ahead, check pet fees, leash rules, quiet hours and night temperatures, and keep your dog with you day and night, never tied up or alone in a tent. Store food away from wildlife, restrain them in the car, and keep ID on.
completion: Your dog has tried the kit as they chose and the trip bag holds only what they accepted, with a luggage tag.
photoIdea: Your dog at the open shelter door, looking out, taken from behind or the side.
memoryPrompt: Which piece of gear got your dog's approval first, and which one stayed home?
supplies: A sleeping mat or folded blanket
A bag and a luggage tag or card
substitutes: Two chairs and a blanket instead of a tent
A flashlight with a cloth over it instead of a lantern

reservation.note: The rehearsal needs nothing booked. The campsite upgrade needs a dog-welcoming pitch or cabin booked ahead.

safety: Never zip your dog in or leave them alone in a tent; use an outdoor tent only in shade and mild weather.
Use LED lights only, no flames, stoves or heaters, and keep stakes and guy lines out of paths.
For a real campsite, check leash and food-storage rules, keep ID on and restrain your dog in the car.
